title: Sensex Plunges 813 Points to Three-Month Low as Brent Crude Surges Past $100
excerpt: Indian benchmarks fell for a third consecutive session as escalating US-Iran hostilities pushed oil prices above $100 a barrel, triggering broad-based selling across sectors.
body:
• Sensex closed 813 points lower at 74,764 while Nifty fell 204 points to 23,432 — both at their lowest levels since June 11
  • Brent crude surged above $100 a barrel for the first time since late July after Iran fired missiles at a US base in Jordan and attacked 10 ships
  • IT stocks led the decline with a 3.2% drop, while the rupee fell 21 paise to 94.95 against the dollar
  • India VIX spiked 7% to 11.92, signalling elevated market uncertainty ahead of US inflation data

Indian equity markets suffered their steepest single-session decline in over a month on Wednesday, with the Sensex and Nifty tumbling to three-month lows as Brent crude breached the psychologically critical $100-a-barrel mark for the first time since late July.

The BSE Sensex closed 813.35 points, or 1.08 percent, lower at 74,764.23, while the broader Nifty 50 shed 203.60 points, or 0.86 percent, to settle at 23,431.50. Both benchmarks logged their lowest closing levels since June 11, extending losses into a third consecutive session.

Middle East Escalation Drives Oil Spike

The selloff was triggered by a sharp escalation in the six-month-old conflict in the Middle East. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired ballistic missiles at a US military base in Jordan and attacked 10 ships on Wednesday, hours after Washington confirmed it had destroyed five Iranian oil tankers.

Brent crude, the global benchmark, climbed above $100 a barrel, while WTI crude held in the $94–95 range. The spike renewed fears of widening trade deficits, imported inflation, and constrained monetary policy for oil-dependent economies like India.

"For India, sustained crude prices around or above $100 could intensify inflationary pressures, weigh on the rupee and the current account, squeeze corporate margins and diminish expectations of monetary easing."

— Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO, HST Wealth

IT Stocks Lead the Rout

Information technology stocks bore the heaviest losses, with the Nifty IT index sliding 3.2 percent. Coforge tumbled 5.4 percent after Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt resigned following concerns raised by an internal audit over the company's board evaluation process.

The sector faced additional pressure as investors awaited US inflation data due later this week, which could determine whether the Federal Reserve raises interest rates at its meeting next week. Higher US rates typically weigh on technology spending, a key revenue driver for India's IT exporters.

Rupee Weakens, Volatility Spikes

The Indian rupee depreciated 21 paise to 94.95 against the US dollar, weighed down by surging oil prices and risk-off sentiment. The fear gauge India VIX jumped 7 percent to 11.92, reflecting heightened uncertainty across the market.

Foreign institutional investors turned net sellers on September 8, offloading equities worth Rs 123.19 crore, adding to the downward pressure on domestic markets.

Market breadth was decisively negative, with 2,382 stocks declining against 1,805 advances on the BSE.

Energy and Metal Stocks Buck the Trend

Not all sectors were in the red. Energy stocks rose 0.6 percent and metal stocks gained 1.8 percent, benefiting from the commodity price surge. Graphite India climbed more than 13 percent to a near eight-year high after global graphite electrode leader GrafTech International announced a 30 percent minimum price hike.

Adani Enterprises gained 5.1 percent after announcing a $1 billion stake sale in its airport unit to a consortium of global investors.

What Comes Next

Analysts flagged the 23,300 level on the Nifty as a crucial support zone. A sustained break below that could accelerate the decline toward 23,150, while resistance sits near 23,620–23,640.

"Oil remains the principal macro driver. With no clear signs of de-escalation, the geopolitical risk premium embedded in crude prices is expected to remain elevated, keeping volatility across global financial markets high."

— Ponmudi R, CEO, Enrich Money

All eyes now turn to this week's US inflation data, which could shape expectations for the Federal Reserve's rate decision and set the tone for global risk appetite in the near term.
